covers.quote: In referencing, present shortened forms in roman type (not italics).

rules.violation_condition: A shortened form used in referencing is set in italics rather than roman type.
when: Applies to shortened forms used in referencing.
rules.why: G-4: the heading and first body sentence state the same typography rule.

rules.quote: Always start them with a lower case letter, even when they are derived from Latin words.
rules.specification: The general instruction conflicts with the table's capitalised MS and MSS. Treat those explicitly listed forms as exceptions; this exception is inferred from the table rather than expressly stated.
rules.violation_condition: A shortened form used in referencing starts with an upper-case letter, other than the table-listed forms MS and MSS.
when: Applies to shortened forms used in referencing, including those derived from Latin.
Treat MS and MSS as exceptions because the table explicitly presents them in capitals.
rules.why: G-1: capitalisation is a separate check from typography, despite appearing beneath the typography heading. G-2: the table-listed exception stays within this rule.

rules.quote: Only some Latin shortened forms and ‘n.d.’ take full stops.
rules.violation_condition: A shortened form used in referencing contains an abbreviation full stop that is not present in its table-listed spelling.
when: Applies to shortened forms used in referencing.
The table permits abbreviation full stops in c., cf., et al., et seq., ibid., id., inf., loc. cit., n.d., op. cit. and sup.
Distinguish abbreviation full stops from punctuation ending the surrounding sentence.
rules.why: G-2: the table identifies the permitted cases for one full-stop check; its entries are not separate rules.

covers.quote: Avoid Latin shortened forms in referencing systems
The terms ‘ibid.’, ‘op. cit.’, ‘loc. cit.’ and ‘id.’ are sometimes used in the documentary–note system and other styles of referencing.

rules.quote: These terms should be avoided unless they are required by a publisher.
rules.violation_condition: A reference uses ibid., op. cit., loc. cit. or id. without a publisher requirement to use that term.
when: Applies specifically to ibid., op. cit., loc. cit. and id. in referencing.
The terms are permitted when required by a publisher.
rules.why: G-4: the body gives the actionable scope more precisely than the heading. G-2 and G-3: the publisher requirement is an exception, not another rule.
